target.title: Harden jq safe-bin module semantics
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Operators can explicitly opt `jq` into exec safe-bin mode for stdin-oriented JSON filters. The existing semantic check denied direct environment reads, but module-loading jq programs could still pull code from jq's module search path and run it without going through an explicit allowlist entry or approval prompt.

## Why This Change Was Made

This change extends the jq safe-bin semantic gate to deny module-loading directives in the jq program token. It keeps benign field access such as `.include` and `.import` valid, while requiring module-based jq programs to use an explicit allowlist entry or approval-gated execution.

## User Impact

Simple jq filters that operate on stdin continue to work when `jq` is configured as a safe bin. jq programs that use `include` or `import` no longer qualify for approval-free safe-bin execution and will need an explicit allowlist path or an approval prompt.

AI-assisted: yes.

## Evidence

- `git diff --check`
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/exec-safe-bin-semantics.test.ts src/infra/exec-approvals-safe-bins.test.ts`
  - Local fallback used because Testbox/Crabbox was unavailable in this environment: installed `crabbox` is `0.20.0`, while the Testbox wrapper requires a newer binary; direct AWS fallback also lacked broker configuration.
  - Result: 2 Vitest shards passed, 62 tests passed.
